names.pk_Server: The server's public key, carried in the end-entity certificate of its Certificate message and used to verify its CertificateVerify signature (§4.4.2, §4.4.3).
names.sk_Server: The server's private signing key, matching the public key in its end-entity certificate, with which it signs CertificateVerify (§4.4.2, §4.4.3).
names.PSK: The pre-shared key in use, either established externally or derived from the resumption_master_secret of a previous connection, input to HKDF-Extract to form the Early Secret (zero if no PSK is used) (§2.2, §4.6.1, §7.1).
names.server_certificates: The identity scope of the server identities clients authenticate through certificates chaining to their trust anchors; open means the attacker may obtain a valid certificate for a server identity of its own (§4.4.2, §4.4.2.2).
names.psk_identities: The identity scope of the PSKs clients and servers share, external or established through NewSessionTicket, which a client names by a PskIdentity in its pre_shared_key extension and a server accepts after validating the binder; open means the attacker shares PSKs of its own with honest endpoints (§2.2, §4.2.11).
names.dh_group: The (EC)DHE group of the key exchange, one of the named groups of the client's supported_groups for which it sends a key_share, answered by the server's key_share in its ServerHello (§4.2.7, §4.2.8).
names.hash_algorithm: The cipher suite hash algorithm, used by Transcript-Hash and HKDF and so for the transcript hash the server signs in CertificateVerify (§7.1, §4.4.1, §4.4.3, §B.4).
names.aead_algorithm: The AEAD algorithm of the negotiated cipher suite, which protects the records; for 0-RTT data, that of the cipher suite associated with the PSK (§5.2, §4.2.10, §B.4).
names.Client: The client, the endpoint initiating the TLS connection (§1.1).
names.Server: The server, the endpoint which did not initiate the TLS connection (§1.1).
names.random_Client: ClientHello.random, the client's 32 bytes from a secure random number generator (§4.1.2).
names.random_Server: ServerHello.random, the server's 32 bytes from a secure random number generator (§4.1.3).
names.offer_Client: The client's offer in its ClientHello for the parameters the server will select: the protocol versions, the cipher suites (AEAD algorithm and hash), the key-exchange groups with key_share, and the PSK and its psk_key_exchange_modes (§4.1.1, §4.1.2).
names.selected_parameters_Server: The parameters the server selects from the offer in its ServerHello: the version, the cipher_suite (AEAD algorithm and hash), the key-exchange group of its key_share, and whether and which PSK is used (§4.1.1, §4.1.3).
names.application_write_key_Client: The client application traffic key, client_write_key derived with HKDF-Expand-Label from client_application_traffic_secret_0 (§7.1, §7.3).
names.application_write_key_Server: The server application traffic key, server_write_key derived with HKDF-Expand-Label from server_application_traffic_secret_0 (§7.1, §7.3).
names.exporter_master_secret: exporter_master_secret, Derive-Secret(Master Secret, "exp master", ClientHello...server Finished), the secret behind keying material exporters (§7.1, §7.5).
names.per_record_nonce: The per-record nonce of the AEAD-protected record carrying the data, the padded 64-bit sequence number XORed with the sender's write_iv (§5.3).
names.additional_data: The AEAD additional data input of a protected record, the record header TLSCiphertext.opaque_type || TLSCiphertext.legacy_record_version || TLSCiphertext.length (§5.2).
names.application_data_Client: The client's 1-RTT application data (TLSInnerPlaintext.content of a record of type application_data), sent after its Finished under keys derived from client_application_traffic_secret_N (§2, §5.2, §7.3).
names.early_data_Client: The client's 0-RTT early data, application data sent in its first flight under keys from client_early_traffic_secret, whose security properties the document calls weaker than those of other TLS data (§2.3, §4.2.10, §7.3).

goals.name: tls13-rfc8446-only.auth_client_to_server_handshake_noninj
goals.description: In the reftls model of RFC 8446, where every handshake uses a PSK with (EC)DHE and the server also authenticates with its certificate (a combination the RFC does not specify, §2.2, §E.1), when the client completes a 1-RTT handshake, a server reached its Finished with the same randoms, PSK, server public key, offered and selected parameters, application traffic keys and exporter_master_secret.

goals.name: tls13-rfc8446-only.secrecy_client_traffic_key_1rtt
goals.description: In the reftls model of RFC 8446, where every handshake uses a PSK with (EC)DHE and the server also authenticates with its certificate (a combination the RFC does not specify, §2.2, §E.1), the attacker never learns the client application traffic key of a handshake the client completed.

goals.name: tls13-rfc8446-only.auth_client_to_server_handshake
goals.description: In the reftls model of RFC 8446, where every handshake uses a PSK with (EC)DHE and the server also authenticates with its certificate (a combination the RFC does not specify, §2.2, §E.1), when the client completes a 1-RTT handshake, a distinct server run reached its Finished with the same randoms, PSK, server public key, offered and selected parameters, application traffic keys and exporter_master_secret.

goals.name: tls13-rfc8446-only.secrecy_client_earlydata_0rtt
goals.description: In the reftls model of RFC 8446, where every handshake uses a PSK with (EC)DHE and the server also authenticates with its certificate (a combination the RFC does not specify, §2.2, §E.1), the attacker never learns the client's 0-RTT early data.

goals.name: tls13-rfc8446-only.auth_server_receives_appdata
goals.description: In the reftls model of RFC 8446, where every handshake uses a PSK with (EC)DHE and the server also authenticates with its certificate (a combination the RFC does not specify, §2.2, §E.1), when the server accepts a client 1-RTT record, the client sent that data in a session with the same randoms, PSK and server public key, under the same per-record nonce and additional data (replay is left to the receiver refusing a repeated nonce).

goals.name: tls13-rfc8446-only.auth_server_receives_earlydata_0rtt
goals.description: In the reftls model of RFC 8446, where every handshake uses a PSK with (EC)DHE and the server also authenticates with its certificate (a combination the RFC does not specify, §2.2, §E.1), when the server accepts 0-RTT early data, the client sent it in a session with the same ClientHello.random and PSK, under the same per-record nonce and additional data (non-injective: 0-RTT data can be replayed).

unexpressed.why: unexpressed point: missing assumption: the server key and the PSK of the tested session are not both compromised. The query (the client application key leak event) excuses a session only when its server key is the attacker's (WeakOrCompromisedKey) and its PSK is compromised or absent (every session of this model uses a PSK), so either credential alone must protect it: the conjunction of the points 'sk_Server disclosed, PSK none' and 'PSK disclosed, sk_Server none', which no single point expresses. Other conditions: the attacker can register server keys and create PSKs of its own, which honest clients and servers use (server_certificates and psk_identities open); a weak (EC)DHE group chosen for the tested session is excepted (dh_group ideal); a weak hash is not excepted (hash_algorithm weak_member); a weak AEAD algorithm is not excepted (aead_algorithm weak_member).
